verdict.reasoning: Patient says she has been feeling this way "maybe about two months or so" and later repeats symptoms have worsened "over the past couple of months."
She states symptoms "probably coincides with, me starting a new job" and describes it as "really stressful" working "for a... fashion retailer, in... the head office team."

She goes to bed at "ten, eleven" but is "lying awake all night" and wakes early with "my heart kind of racing" before her alarm. She estimates "maybe, three, four hours" of sleep and describes it as "such a shallow sleep."

Palpitations are described as occurring in the morning when she fears being late, "a constant like, rapid heart beating"; she says it feels "Irregular, I think" and can last "couple of minutes" to "like ten minutes." She denies chest pain except "it's painful... when my heart is beating fast" (discomfort with tachycardia, not distinct chest pain).

She reports "really, really low" energy, finds "no enjoyment at all" in day-to-day life, is "on edge the whole time," avoids going out with friends as she knows she's "not gonna have fun," and says she used to go running and play tennis but is "not going out to do that quite so much."
She says "I find public transport really stressful anyway, especially being on the tube it's, 'cause it's quite, getting warmer so it's just really airless."

She denies past similar episodes: "I've never felt, anything this bad before." When asked about panic attacks she answers "No I wouldn't say so" and adds she's worried "it's building up to that... I've felt it get worse and worse over the past couple of months."
She states she is "pretty much, down" and that even at weekends there is a "constant, feeling of just being a bit, down, a bit unhappy."
She says "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts" and notes "I have a good support system, like I do have good family and stuff."

Regarding eating, she says "Probably, not, significant changes" and "I wouldn't say that I'm eating like, much differently," but adds "I probably have more chocolate than normal, just because I feel, so down."
When asked who she lives with, she replies "Yeah, I live with my parents, just my parents."

She describes "probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday... going out, so maybe like. I probably go over my limit just on those days" and also mentions "maybe a glass of wine during the week" and that she doesn't really keep track.
She states "I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally, but I don't take drugs."
She says she talks to her mum "because she also suffers from, well she's, suffered from like depression in the past."

Transcript describes work-focused anxiety for "about two months," with insomnia and palpitations, impacting sleep (3–4 hours shallow sleep), socializing (avoids friends) and hobbies (reduced running and tennis), and she explicitly denies suicidal thoughts.

She links low mood and lack of enjoyment to ongoing stress and anxiety about work and life and notes "I have a good support system, like I do have good family and stuff," consistent with low mood/anhedonia secondary to anxiety with supportive family.
Doctor says palpitations are "most likely... associated with anxiety"; she describes an "Irregular, I think" feeling and denies distinct chest pain, only discomfort when her heart is fast.
Doctor says she can self-refer via the NHS "for what we call like, talking therapy" (a CBT-type therapy) and adds "I can send you the link for that."
Doctor states "There are some online resources that are really helpful. Um, can put the details, on there and you can, get on with them straight away."
Doctor says "I'll put some more information on your notes about, helping with your, sleep patterns and things like that."

Doctor advises that if it's "not helping at all, or your anxiety is getting worse, to the point where you can't cope with work, or you can't, just do your normal things day-to-day. Then, it's important... to give us a call, back and just discuss that, further."
Doctor notes "some people, with anxiety they, do need to take medication... but that's, not something that we'd suggest in the first instance," implying medication is second-line if needed.
Doctor says it's "probably worth having couple of basic blood tests" and instructs, "if you call the support line you can arrange the, to have the blood test done."
Doctor plans "arranging a GP follow-up a week after you've had the tests, so we can just go through the results with you."
No advice about moderating alcohol or weekend binges is documented; alcohol is only elicited in history without explicit counseling.
There is no mention of encouraging return to exercise or advice about resuming running or tennis in the transcript.
The transcript does not include any advice on smoking cessation or resources; smoking is only asked about in history.
